definitions.explanation: A breeze or wind that blows at night. Often evokes a cool, pleasant, or atmospheric feeling.

examples.japanese: {夜風|よかぜ}が{気持|きも}ちいい。
{夜風|よかぜ}に{当|あ}たりながら{散歩|さんぽ}した。
examples.english: I took a walk in the night breeze.

examples.japanese: {窓|まど}を{開|あ}けると、{涼|すず}しい{夜風|よかぜ}が{部屋|へや}に{入|はい}ってきた。
examples.english: When I opened the window, a cool night breeze came into the room.

notes:
Compound of {夜|よ} (night) + {風|かぜ} (wind, breeze). A poetic and evocative word frequently found in literature, song lyrics, and seasonal descriptions.

USAGE:
Often appears with verbs like {当|あ}たる (to be exposed to) and {吹|ふ}く (to blow). Carries a literary or atmospheric tone, evoking scenes of quiet nighttime moments. Especially associated with summer evenings when the night air brings welcome relief from daytime heat.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {夜風|よかぜ}に{当|あ}たる — to feel the night breeze
- {夜風|よかぜ}が{吹|ふ}く — the night breeze blows
- {涼|すず}しい{夜風|よかぜ} — cool night breeze
- {冷|つめ}たい{夜風|よかぜ} — cold night wind

SIMILAR WORDS:
- そよ{風|かぜ} — gentle breeze (not time-specific)
- {朝風|あさかぜ} — morning breeze
- {涼風|りょうふう}/すずかぜ — cool breeze (not time-specific)
